Subject: Purchase order & invoice cadence for Redwood platform (RDW-9247)

Vivek,

Following up from last week's exec call — procurement at Acme needs to confirm a few things before we can issue a blanket PO:

- PO format: must include Acme cost-center mapping (we'll attach a sample PO).
- Invoice cadence: preferred is monthly invoices tied to usage, but finance has asked whether you can accept split invoices (25% milestone up front, 75% monthly) on annual commitments.
- Net terms: standard for us is net60, but pending approval we could consider net90 for first year only.

Can you confirm Redwood can: accept a single blanket PO referencing multiple cost centers; issue monthly usage invoices; and provide a credit/adjustment process if monthly usage dips below threshold? Also please share a final SOW and an editable PO template.

Thanks,
John
John Reynolds
Director, Procurement — Acme Systems
procurement@acmesystems.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@getredwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Purchase order & invoice cadence for Redwood platform (RDW-9247)

John —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front: yes to blanket PO referencing multiple cost centers, yes to monthly usage invoices. On split invoices and net terms, we have some flexibility but need to align on discounting and finance approvals.

Details:
- PO & cost centers: we can map invoice line-items to cost-center IDs if you include them on the PO. Please use the attached Redwood_PO_Template.pdf — it has the fields our billing system uses.
- Invoice cadence & split: we can support an initial milestone invoice (up to 30% at contract signature) with monthly usage invoices afterward. If you need 25%/75% we can accommodate, but that will affect the discount matrix.
- Net terms: standard hosted customer terms are net30; for enterprise commitments we can extend to net45 or net60 with appropriate credit approval. Net90 would require an underwriting exception and a short-term credit hold.
- Credits & adjustments: we provide a monthly credit memo process for over/under usage; if monthly usage drops below an agreed floor we issue a pro-rated credit the next billing cycle.

I've attached the SOW draft (SOW-RDW-9247-v2.docx) and a pricing worksheet — Marissa, Ben, can you confirm what discount we can offer for a 12-month blanket PO with the requested split and net60?

Next steps I propose:
1) Acme sends sample PO with cost center mapping.
2) Redwood issues final SOW and editable PO template (attached).
3) Finance sync: Marissa/Ben and Acme finance to align on net terms and discount.

Best,
Vivek
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Vivek / John —

Thanks for laying this out. From a commercial perspective here are a couple of negotiation points that typically close quickly:

- Discounting: for a 12-month committed spend we can do a 15% list discount if Acme is willing to accept net45 and up to 30% upfront. If Acme insists on net60 and smaller upfront, discount steps down to ~10%.
- Billing floor: we need an agreed monthly minimum to avoid repeated credits; we typically set a 20% of the committed ARR floor for crediting.
- PO references: we can accept a single blanket PO with cost-center lines, but the PO must include the Redwood legal entity (Redwood Inference, Inc.) and the billing address exactly as in the template.

Ben will follow up with Finance to see what documentation is needed for a net60 exception. John — can you share the sample PO and internal credit approval SLA (how long procurement needs to approve exceptions)?

Marissa
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@getredwood.ai

Marissa —

Thanks. Attaching our sample PO (procurement@acmesystems.com). Our standard SLA for credit/term exceptions is 10 business days; net90 would be a stretch but we can escalate to treasury for a one-time window. The PO will reference multiple cost centers — we expect line-level accounting codes.

A few clarifications from our side:
- If Redwood requires a 30% upfront to hit 15% discount, treasury will want a clause that unused prepayments convert to monthly credits automatically.
- We prefer invoicing to go to ap@acmesystems.com and for remittance details to be on the invoice PDF (our AR platform ingests PDFs).
- Can you confirm whether Redwood supports sending invoices via SFTP/EDI mapping? That would help our AP automation.

John

John —

We can support EDI/SFTP invoice delivery; I will have our billing ops send the spec and SFTP endpoint details. On net terms: to get to net60 we need a standard credit form and a PO referencing the Redwood legal entity. For net90 we will need a short form credit review (1–2 business days once we have the PO and 12 months of projected usage).

On the commercial ask: Marissa's 15% for 12 months + 30% upfront + net45 is the baseline that hits our pricing model. If Acme must have net60, we can offer 12% instead of 15% or accept 15% with an additional 30-day payment hold on initial milestone until treasury approves.

I will upload the billing spec and send a quantized proposal showing the monthly invoice and credit mech. Expect that by EOD Thu.
